bull_bear.body:
- Net debt **INR 9,290 cr**, D/E 0.63; mgmt prioritises debt reduction but cautiously.
- Debt structure: **NCDs INR 3,260 cr** (next due 2028, locked till then); **ECB $500M (~INR 4,500 cr)** — repayment is a forex trade-off (FX loss if repaid early; awaiting US-trade-deal-driven INR strength).
- Capital allocation framed as 3-way trade-off: own capex vs debt vs dividend.
- Dividend possible after profitable Q4 (board decision).
bull_bear.title: Capital Allocation (deleveraging)

bull_bear.body:
- **GRM / crack volatility:** Q3 EBITDA is crack-cycle peak; cracks already down ~30% to $14–15. Earnings highly sensitive to refining-margin cycle; GRM opacity (no disclosure) reduces visibility.
- **Sanctions / crude re-sourcing:** 18th EU sanctions package (effective ~21-Jan) and evolving regime; mgmt "compliant," no Russian crude — but sourcing/freight uncertainty "not going away immediately."
- **Petrochem cycle / execution:** IBB years from commercialisation; legacy PP/PX exposed to petchem down-cycle; no near-term contribution.
- **Leverage / forex:** ~INR 9,300 cr debt; ECB repayment carries forex risk; debt reduction "not very significant" near-term.
- **Valuation / float:** ~88% held by ONGC + HPCL, only ~12% public float (≈1% locked) — a structural overhang on re-rating; PSU OMC valuations depressed on perceived government control of pricing/taxation (e.g. SAED precedent).
- **Freight rates:** Spiked in Q3 (Middle East tensions), eased but still above Q1.
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and notably candid. CFO Devendra Kumar openly acknowledged Q3 cracks/GRM are unsustainable ("market will not be able to sustain"), volunteered the float/valuation problem unprompted ("a question we also ask ourselves"), and was transparent that Russian barrels were always marginal. Promotional on the retail-marketing pivot and ATF/CORSIA leadership. Repeatedly declined to put numbers on GRM, IBB IRR, and exact debt trajectory — guarded on forward specifics while bullish on the structural marketing story. Warm, investor-friendly close (open invitation to visit the refinery).
bull_bear.title: Mgmt Tone

bull_bear.body:
- **GRM withheld is the key tell:** with GRM/inventory undisclosed, the headline INR 2,824 cr EBITDA cannot be decomposed — it is implicitly a crack-cycle peak (cracks already back to Q2 levels), so do NOT annualise Q3.
- **Russian-crude exit is a non-event:** mgmt insists product cracks rose far more than the lost Russian discount, so the sanctions hit is net positive for Q3 margins — counter-intuitive vs the usual "loss of cheap crude hurts PSU refiners" narrative.
- **Net vs gross throughput:** the 4.7 vs 4.56 MMT "discrepancy" is just net-vs-gross crude (the ~10% F&L), not an error.
- **Float, not fundamentals, caps the stock:** mgmt explicitly blames ~88% promoter holding (ONGC + HPCL) + perceived government price/tax control for the depressed ~INR 25,000 cr market cap vs ~INR 7,000–10,000 cr/MMT replacement cost on 15 MMTPA — they are examining the low-float issue WITH the parent.
- **Retail is still tiny** (~1.5–2% of volumes) — the marketing thesis is multi-year optionality, not current earnings.
- **IBB / Bio-ATF** are long-dated, sub-scale (pilot / INR 364 cr) — narrative/ESG flavour more than near-term P&L.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Dominant position in the institutional business segment of the petroleum and petrochemicals products market across Karnataka and adjoining states
- Crude flexibility — access to a diversified crude basket of 273 crude grades sourced globally, with more than 116 crude varieties processed over the years, providing operational flexibility and supply resilience
- High asset utilisation — 111.8% capacity utilisation and 81.94% distillate yield in FY2025-26 despite a planned Phase-II shutdown
- Parentage and CPSE status — Schedule "A" Mini Ratna PSU and subsidiary of ONGC, with HPCL also a promoter and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas as administrative ministry
- Coastal logistics — location adjacent to the New Mangalore Port Authority, with a record 13 Very Large Crude Carriers handled in FY2025-26
- Evacuation infrastructure — record 4.07 MMT of auto fuels and ATF dispatched through the Petronet MHB Limited (PMHBL) pipeline in Karnataka
- Growing owned retail channel — 252 fully operational HiQ outlets as on 31 March 2026 across four southern states
- Aviation fuel access through the 50% Shell MRPL Aviation Fuel and Services Limited joint venture, expanding market share across several airports
- Asset-light downstream marketing model using third-party terminals to widen reach while optimising capital deployment
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Climate change adaptation, resilience and transition — Flagged in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Key risks are potential operational disruptions from extreme weather events, resource constraints such as water availability, evolving regulatory requirements and significant capital needs associated with energy transition, given the Company's reliance on fossil fuels. Mitigation is through operational resilience measures, regulatory compliance and transition planning, phased investments in energy efficiency and gradual portfolio diversification. Financial implications stated as positive as well as negative.
- GHG emissions and energy management — Non-compliance with GHG emission norms presents legal, financial and reputational risks including exposure to carbon pricing mechanisms, penalties and significant capital requirements for compliance and transition. Rising energy costs and stricter emission standards may also impact operating margins. Addressed through continuous emissions monitoring, energy efficiency initiatives, equipment and process upgrades, best-available technologies and integrating emissions considerations into capital planning.
- Air quality management — A material risk given the nature of refinery operations and associated SOx, NOx, particulate matter and VOC emissions. Non-compliance with evolving air quality standards could result in regulatory penalties, operational restrictions or shutdowns, reputational impacts and adverse effects on surrounding communities. Increasingly stringent norms require continuous monitoring, process optimisation and ongoing investment in cleaner fuels and emission-control technologies. Financial implication stated as negative.
- Water availability and water stewardship — Water availability is named as a resource constraint within the climate risk rationale; the BRSR separately identifies water management as an opportunity requiring maximised wastewater recycling, reduced freshwater consumption and advanced water technologies to lower water intensity and strengthen long-term operational resilience.
- Board composition non-compliance and dependence on the administrative ministry for director appointments — The Company did not meet SEBI requirements for Board composition due to a shortfall in Independent Directors during FY2025-26; after four Independent Directors including the Independent Woman Director completed tenure on 27/03/2026, the Board and all sub-committees — Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship, Risk Management and CSR — fell short of composition requirements from 28/03/2026 to 31/03/2026. Appointment of directors is handled by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, so remediation is outside the Company's direct control. The Secretarial Auditors made an observation on this.
- Single-activity and product concentration — The entirety of the Company's turnover comes from one activity — crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals — with High-Speed Diesel and Motor Spirit the dominant products, leaving earnings fully exposed to refining margins and auto-fuel demand with no diversifying business line.
- Export dependence and geographic concentration of the marketing footprint — A significant share of turnover is exported, exposing the Company to global product cracks and trade disruption, while domestically its institutional dominance and its HiQ retail network are concentrated in Karnataka and adjoining southern states served from a single Mangaluru manufacturing site.
- Single-site operational and shutdown exposure — All refining and petrochemicals manufacturing sits at the Mangaluru complex; the planned Phase-II Refinery M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit in May-June 2025 illustrates how maintenance or an unplanned outage at one site directly interrupts throughput and dispatch.

business.body: MRPL's main activity is crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals, described in the BRSR as "Manufacturing & marketing of petroleum and petrochemicals products" accounting for 100% of turnover. latest_quarter.body:
- **GRM:** Crack-driven, not absolute-price driven ("we are marked-to-market; margins come from cracks"). Q3 cracks peaked (HSD $21) then normalised to $14–15. GRM no longer published.

latest_quarter.body: - **Q3 FY26 (this call):** EBITDA INR 2,824 cr (YoY +165% vs 1,064 cr) on peak cracks (HSD $21, MS $13) — already moderated to ~$14–15. GRM NOT published (discontinued from Q2; indicative ~2x Q1). Throughput 4.7 MMT net (~18 MMT annualised, ~120% nameplate). F&L 10.06% (best-ever; grid power → 9.5–10% next FY). Net debt INR 9,290 cr, D/E 0.63 (NCDs 3,260 cr due 2028; ECB $500M). Zero Russian crude; ~40% Middle East; ~70–72% heavy (9M); ~40% exports. Retail 200→250 (FY26-end)→500 (3yr)→1,000 (5yr), ~2% of vol, ~120 KL/mo/outlet, ~INR 2 cr/outlet. Capex ~1,500 cr/yr (887 cr 9M; 400–450 cr growth). Dividend possible post-Q4. IBB pilot (3–4 yrs out); Bio-ATF INR 364 cr (CORSIA 2027). Float overhang flagged (~88% ONGC+HPCL).

outlook.body:
- **GRM / cracks:** Will NOT publish GRM. Current cracks ~$14–15 (down from Q3 $21), i.e. **Q2-like trajectory** — Q4 expected "reasonably healthy" but not a Q3 repeat ("very high GRMs market will not sustain").
- **Throughput:** Targeting ~18 MMT annualised run-rate (~120% nameplate); past summer "water blues" (desalination plant) resolved.
- **Petrochem ramp:** IBB (Isobutyl Benzene, pharma intermediate) **pilot** only — commercialisation **3–4 years away**, multiple decision gates; IRR "too early to comment." No near-term petchem earnings.
- **Retail-outlet rollout (KEY):** 200 today → **250 by FY26-end** → **500 in 3 years** → **1,000 in 5 years** (called "conservative/intermediate"). ~120 KL/month/outlet; avg outlet cost ~INR 2 cr (range INR 1.5 cr rural to higher urban). Retail currently only ~**1.5–2%** of volumes/revenue.
- **Capex:** **~INR 1,500 cr/yr** FY26 AND FY27 (similar); INR 887 cr spent in 9M, ramps to ~1,500 cr by Mar; split ~**INR 400–450 cr growth** (retail, grid power, IBB) / rest maintenance & revamp.
- **Marketing infra:** Depots ~INR 50–100 cr each/yr; pipelines ~INR 200 cr (Mumbai, Vizag, Kerala, Bangalore-airport pipeline tender pending); ~INR 500 cr ± near-term marketing infra.
- **Dividend:** Possible — board may consider after a profitable Q4; "on the anvil," subject to capex + debt + payout balance.
- **Bio-ATF:** INR 364 cr plant; CORSIA-compliant blended ATF (1% blend) supply from **2027**.

outlook.body:
- Q3 throughput 4.7 MMT (net) / 4.56 MMT (gross PPAC) — discrepancy = net vs gross crude (revenue driven by net).
- Annualised ~18 MMT, ~120% of 15 MMTPA nameplate; unique 3-separate-crude-train design gives operational/maintenance flexibility (at cost of slightly higher F&L).

outlook.title: Growth / Optionality

outlook.body:
- Remain focused on operational excellence, energy security, financial resilience and sustainable value creation
- Ensure uninterrupted refinery operations through diversified crude sourcing, effective inventory management and operational agility
- Strengthen the Company's position as a key contributor to India's energy landscape through disciplined operations, prudent planning and technological adoption
- Pursue with the administrative ministry (MoP&NG) the appointment of the requisite number of Independent Directors, including an Independent Woman Director, to restore compliance with Board composition requirements
- Continue CSR and sustainable development activity under the "SAMRAKSHAN" brand, governed by a CSR & SD Policy aligned to Schedule VII of the Companies Act and DPE guidelines
- MRPL has a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy published on its website, alongside a Material Subsidiary Policy, Board Diversity Policy, Whistle Blower Policy and a Policy on Remuneration of Directors, KMP and Other Employees. For FY2025-26 the Board declared an interim dividend on equity shares and recommended the same as the final dividend, described as reflecting the Company's continued commitment to shareholder value creation; the interim dividend was declared at the Board meeting of 03/03/2026 with a record date of 11/03/2026 and is placed at the 38th AGM for confirmation as the final dividend. Form AOC-1 Part A records "NOT APPLICABLE" for subsidiaries — the Company has none — so all equity investment outside the refinery sits in the 50% SMAFSL joint venture. Reinvestment is directed at strengthening refining operations, expanding the HiQ marketing presence (including an asset-light third-party-terminal model to optimise capital deployment), value addition and future energy opportunities such as Bio-ATF, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, Green Hydrogen and value-added petrochemical products, guided by a Net-Zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2038 ambition. As a Central Public Sector Enterprise, MRPL follows the Corporate Governance Guidelines for CPSEs issued by DPE in addition to the SEBI Listing Regulations.
- Climate transition managed through phased investments in energy efficiency, emissions reduction initiatives and gradual portfolio diversification, with regulatory developments monitored to ensure compliance
- Diversification into lower-carbon products such as biofuels and green hydrogen identified as the climate transition opportunity
- Continuous monitoring of GHG emissions, optimisation of fuel and energy usage, upgrading of equipment and processes, adoption of best-available technologies, and integration of emissions considerations into capital planning
- Air quality managed through continuous emissions monitoring, operation of pollution control systems across refinery units, regular maintenance and upgrading of emission-control equipment, use of cleaner fuels, process optimisation and ambient air quality monitoring within and around operational areas
- Water stewardship targeting maximised wastewater recycling, reduced freshwater consumption and adoption of advanced water technologies to lower water intensity and support resource diversification
- Clean technology initiatives identified as a material sustainability opportunity
- BRSR Core KPIs subject to reasonable assurance by Bureau Veritas India Private Limited
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place across stakeholder groups — a Whistle Blower Policy for employees and workers, a published complaints mechanism for customers and dealers, SEBI/stock-exchange-governed redressal plus a dedicated investor email for shareholders, and CPGRAMS, the MSME Champions portal and Independent External Monitors for value chain partners
- CSR delivered under the "SAMRAKSHAN" brand pursuant to a CSR & SD Policy aligned to Section 135 and Schedule VII of the Companies Act 2013 and DPE guidelines, with impact assessment of CSR projects published
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: MRPL's FY2025-26 expansion was concentrated in downstream marketing infrastructure and in-refinery debottlenecking/technology upgrades rather than a new refinery train. On the marketing side, the Company commissioned 85 HiQ retail outlets during the year, taking the fully operational network to 252 as on 31 March 2026, and entered Andhra Pradesh with its first outlet there — several further HiQ outlets in Andhra Pradesh are at various stages of construction and commissioning. To support the planned retail expansion it upgraded and modernised depot facilities at Hosur (Tamil Nadu), Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) and Kasaragod (Kerala), commenced operations at third-party terminals in Mangaluru (Karnataka) and Ennore (Tamil Nadu) under an asset-light model, and expanded polypropylene warehousing in Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh. It also signed a deal with ISPRL to lease/rent oil storage capacity of 760 TMT / 5.586 MMBBLs at the ISPRL SPR underground rock cavern at Mangaluru. Inside the refinery, a Phase-II M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit was carried out in May-June 2025; CDU-3 column internals were revamped with tray replacement and coalescer installation for better LPG and lean amine distribution; Divided Wall Column technology (licensor M/s DWC Innovations, USA) was implemented and stabilised in the NSU column of CDU-2; and at the Polypropylene Unit commercial production of two new polypropylene grades (65 MFI TWIM and thermoforming) was completed. Energy-conservation schemes — including Aromatic GT power import, RLNG processing in HGU-3, CDU-2 GAPH replacement, DCU debutaniser pressure reduction, insulation upgrades on HP/MP steam lines and HCU-2 APH replacement — delivered total savings of 43,436 MTOE per annum, and integration of power import from the Aromatic Complex enabled shutdown of the refinery's Steam Turbine Generator and utility boilers. Renewable integration was accelerated through green power procurement via MESCOM/GDAM and in-house solar generation. The Innovation Center, recognised by DSIR, is advancing crude-to-chemicals (GOAT technology, commercialised at scale on a modified Petro-FCC), AI/ML optimisers, API intermediates (Isobutyl Benzene, p-Aminophenol, Salicylic Acid) at lab, mini-pilot and demonstration scale, and plastic circularity — with a PET pilot-cum-demo plant funded by OIDB scheduled to be commissioned within FY 2026-27.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India continued to demonstrate strong economic growth supported by robust domestic demand, infrastructure development, manufacturing activity and industrial expansion
- The country's growing energy requirements reinforce the importance of energy security, supply resilience and operational preparedness
- FY2025-26 was marked by evolving geopolitical developments, volatility in global energy markets and continued focus on energy transition
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: A **blockbuster Q3 driven almost entirely by product cracks**, not crude advantage. EBITDA more than doubled YoY (INR 2,824 cr vs 1,064 cr) as diesel/ATF/MS cracks spiked (HSD ~$15→$21, MS ~$8→$13) amid sanctions-driven market dislocation — more than offsetting the loss of (small, "opportunity") Russian barrels, which MRPL has now fully exited. Best-ever energy efficiency (MBN 67) and fuel-&-loss (10.06%), net debt down to ~INR 9,290 cr (D/E 0.63). Mgmt is candid that the Q3 GRM spike is **not sustainable** — current cracks have already moderated back to ~$14–15 (Q2 levels). The real structural story management is selling is the **pivot from a pure base refinery to a refining-plus-marketing business**: own retail outlets 200 → 250 (FY26-end) → 500 (3yr) → 1,000 (5yr), to capture higher, more stable margins than volatile exports.

open.item: A PET pilot-cum-demo plant for depolymerization of PET and other waste plastics into high-purity monomers, funded by OIDB, is scheduled to be commissioned within FY 2026-27.
MRPL has articulated an ambition of achieving Net Zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions by 2038 and continues to implement a structured roadmap towards this objective.
Several HiQ outlets in Andhra Pradesh are at various stages of construction and commissioning and are expected to further strengthen the Company's retail presence in the region.
The Company is progressing initiatives towards cleaner energy solutions including renewable energy integration, Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), Bio-ATF and Green Hydrogen.
MRPL will remain focused on operational excellence, energy security, financial resilience and sustainable value creation through disciplined operations, prudent planning and technological adoption.

The Company is consistently pursuing with the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas the appointment of the requisite number of Independent Directors, including an Independent Woman Director, to comply with applicable Board and Board sub-committee composition requirements after all Independent Directors ceased office with effect from 28/03/2026.
Unspent CSR amounts were transferred to the Unspent CSR Account on 30/04/2026 and remain to be spent on ongoing projects in succeeding financial years.
Several HiQ retail outlets in Andhra Pradesh are at various stages of construction and commissioning and are expected to further strengthen the Company's retail presence in the region.

The Company will continue to strengthen downstream marketing infrastructure, including operating third-party terminals under an asset-light model to widen market reach while optimising capital deployment.

The Innovation Center will continue to drive strategic R&D across AI/ML, Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients, plastic circularity, net-zero technologies and crude-to-chemicals, with API intermediates at lab, mini-pilot and demonstration scale.

Bulk industrial buyers include Oil Marketing Companies, Indian Railways, State Government Undertakings and other PSUs, road contractors and the mining and cement industries, while retail sales run through MRPL and dealer-owned HiQ …

risks.note: Flagged in the BRSR as both risk and opportunity. Key risks are potential operational disruptions from extreme weather events, resource constraints such as water availability, evolving regulatory requirements and significant capital needs associated with energy transition, given the Company's reliance on fossil fuels. Mitigation is through operational resilience measures, regulatory compliance and transition planning, phased investments in energy efficiency and gradual portfolio diversification. Financial implications stated as positive as well as negative.
risks.risk: Climate change adaptation, resilience and transition

risks.note: Non-compliance with GHG emission norms presents legal, financial and reputational risks including exposure to carbon pricing mechanisms, penalties and significant capital requirements for compliance and transition. Rising energy costs and stricter emission standards may also impact operating margins. Addressed through continuous emissions monitoring, energy efficiency initiatives, equipment and process upgrades, best-available technologies and integrating emissions considerations into capital planning.

A material risk given the nature of refinery operations and associated SOx, NOx, particulate matter and VOC emissions. Non-compliance with evolving air quality standards could result in regulatory penalties, operational restrictions or shutdowns, reputational impacts and adverse effects on surrounding communities. Increasingly stringent norms require continuous monitoring, process optimisation and ongoing investment in cleaner fuels and emission-control technologies. Financial implication stated as negative.

Water availability is named as a resource constraint within the climate risk rationale; the BRSR separately identifies water management as an opportunity requiring maximised wastewater recycling, reduced freshwater consumption and advanced water technologies to lower water intensity and strengthen long-term operational resilience.

The Company did not meet SEBI requirements for Board composition due to a shortfall in Independent Directors during FY2025-26; after four Independent Directors including the Independent Woman Director completed tenure on 27/03/2026, the Board and all sub-committees — Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholders Relationship, Risk Management and CSR — fell short of composition requirements from 28/03/2026 to 31/03/2026. Appointment of directors is handled by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, so remediation is outside the Company's direct control. The Secretarial Auditors made an observation on this.
risks.risk: Board composition non-compliance and dependence on the administrative ministry for director appointments

risks.note: The entirety of the Company's turnover comes from one activity — crude oil refining and manufacturing of petrochemicals — with High-Speed Diesel and Motor Spirit the dominant products, leaving earnings fully exposed to refining margins and auto-fuel demand with no diversifying business line.

A significant share of turnover is exported, exposing the Company to global product cracks and trade disruption, while domestically its institutional dominance and its HiQ retail network are concentrated in Karnataka and adjoining southern states served from a single Mangaluru manufacturing site.
risks.risk: Export dependence and geographic concentration of the marketing footprint

risks.note: All refining and petrochemicals manufacturing sits at the Mangaluru complex; the planned Phase-II Refinery M&I shutdown with catalyst replacement in the CHTU unit in May-June 2025 illustrates how maintenance or an unplanned outage at one site directly interrupts throughput and dispatch.

meta.thesis: A **blockbuster Q3 driven almost entirely by product cracks**, not crude advantage. EBITDA more than doubled YoY (INR 2,824 cr vs 1,064 cr) as diesel/ATF/MS cracks spiked (HSD ~$15→$21, MS ~$8→$13) amid sanctions-driven market dislocation — more than offsetting the loss of (small, "opportunity") Russian barrels, which MRPL has now fully exited. Best-ever energy efficiency (MBN 67) and fuel-&-loss (10.06%), net debt down to ~INR 9,290 cr (D/E 0.63). Mgmt is candid that the Q3 GRM spike is **not sustainable** — current cracks have already moderated back to ~$14–15 (Q2 levels). The real structural story management is selling is the **pivot from a pure base refinery to a refining-plus-marketing business**: own retail outlets 200 → 250 (FY26-end) → 500 (3yr) → 1,000 (5yr), to capture higher, more stable margins than volatile exports.
